articleTitle: A Wearable Temperature Sensor for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable device for IoT applications that accurately measures the body temperature of athletes during exercise. The device is a flexible passive capacitive sensor with a TPU insulator that makes the capacitance dependent on the temperature. This insulator was made with a 3D printer and can be made in any other shape for other applications. A microcontroller reads the sensor's capacitor value by sampling its voltage in an RC series structure and determining its charge time constant. Using a LoRa module, this device transmits the athlete's body temperature from long distances to the server, providing online monitoring of body temperature during exercise. The sensor was tested from 25°C to 45°C to cover athletes' skin temperature variations, showing about a 5% variation in this range. The simulation of the proposed sensor was done in CST Studio Suite, and the measurement results follow the simulation results quite well.

articleTitle: Stripline Temperature Sensor for Passive UHF RFID System
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, the structure of a two-layer stripline sensor with TPU sensitive layer is introduced. TPU is a type of flexible plastic whose dielectric coefficient changes with temperature significantly. The strip-line transmission line with the TPU layer has an effective permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\epsilon_{eff})$</tex> that varies with temperature, and thus the phase constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\beta)$</tex> and the phase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex> change with temperature. The performance of the sensor was based on the measurement of the phase to calculate the temperature.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide-Band Millimeter-Wave CPW-Fed Monopole Antenna for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra wide-band (UWB) co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed millimeter wave (mmWave) antenna is presented. The proposed antenna incorporates modified tilted Vshaped monopole element and unsymmetrical ground planes to increase the impedance and the axial ratio bandwidths. It occupies K and Ka- bands including 24/28 GHz mmWave 5G band with 16 GHz of bandwidth. It operates in a frequency band from 18 GHz to 34 GHz with a circular polarization from 20.6 to 23.3 GHz having 2.7 GHz of 3dB axial ratio bandwidth. Presented UWB antenna is suitable for high data rate mmWave 5G applications. It is designed on semi-flexible substrate making it suitable for wearable applications as well.

articleTitle: A 70-GHz Miniaturized Wideband Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a compact, wideband, and lowcost 4×4 Butler Matrix (BM) for the frequency band of 66 GHz to 71 GHz. The proposed BM is designed based on 100 Ω microstrip lines (MSL) and printed on a single substrate with the total size of 9 mm x 5 mm. The simulation results show an insertion loss ranges from −1 to −4.5 dB with a return loss and mutual coupling lower than −15 dB over the bandwidth of interest. Moreover, a progressive phase delay of ±45° and ±135° between each adjacent output port is achieved for separately exciting the input ports which resulted in four steerable beams at ±15° and ±45°.

articleTitle: 4-Bit Reconfigurable Reflecting Metasurface for Sub-6 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a 4-bit reconfigurable reflecting metasurface for a sub-6-GHz band. A varactor diode with a larger capacitance is embedded in a digital meta atom (unit-cell) to obtain 16 different phase states at 3.5 GHz frequency bands. Furthermore, by installing a digital meta atom in a phase gradient array, a beam can be steered at the desired angle in a reflection mode. The proposed design offering 0° to 360° phase with a step size of 22.5° by varying capactitance range from 0.63pF to 2.67pF. The design is low loss and can maintain angle reciprocity at the proposed operating frequency band. These functionalities make this reconfigurable reflecting metasurface a great candidate for antenna arrays and 6G communications.

articleTitle: Cascaded Wire Metasurfaces for Angular Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Angular filters are structures filtering electromagnetic waves in the spatial domain. Here, a simple periodic structure, morphologically similar to a wire slab is proposed as an angular filter for transverse electric (TE) polarized waves. The structure is modeled as a stack of uniform spatially non-dispersive metasurfaces (MSs) characterized by generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) at various angles of incidence. It is shown that using this semi-analytical modeling approach, the scattering behaviors of such MS stacks can be captured. The merits of the proposed structure amount to flexible design, filtering control and feasible fabrication.

articleTitle: Comparative Investigation of Different Methods of Realization of Anomalous Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Anomalous reflection implemented using metasurfaces is one of the interesting applications, especially for wireless communication networks. Anomalous reflectors have been studied during the last few years and realized based on different design methods. However, the lack of a proper comparison study between these approaches makes it difficult to select the most suitable design based on specific performance requirements. Here, we consider four main design methods for the realization of anomalous reflectors utilizing the same basic geometry of the metasurface structure. First, we compare the methods based on the model of an ideal impedance boundary. Afterwards, we proceed with the comparison of the actual structures realized by patterns of rectangular metal strips on top of a grounded dielectric substrate. We cover a wide range of performance aspects, such as the power efficiency and losses, the angular response, and the scattering pattern of finite-size structures.

articleTitle: Average Active Element Gain Estimates for Rectangular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: An investigation into the convergence of the active element gain for planar arrays is presented. The goal is to evaluate the convergence and accuracy of estimates for the active element gain. The simulation of planar arrays of different sizes shows that the active element gain converges quickly when no grating lobes are present. However, when grating lobes are present, the convergence can be slow and the known estimates can be inaccurate. New estimates are proposed that are more accurate when grating lobes are present.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging for Breast Density Assessment: Initial Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Microwave imaging has been proposed for breast health assessment. The majority of the images of human subjects that have been previously reported focus on tumor detection capabilities. There is a need to correlate additional features of microwave images to clinical information in order to increase confidence in this approach. In this contribution, we present an initial exploration of the connection between the dielectric properties obtained from microwave images and breast density estimates that are readily available from mammography reports.

articleTitle: Disposable Patch Antenna Sensor for Hydration Monitoring to Support Healthy Aging
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Hydration monitoring of elderly adults who require care is a great challenge and can decrease their quality of life. This work aims to introduce a sensing platform for non-invasive hydration level monitoring using urine samples. The proposed sensing platform consists of a patch antenna as a reader and a tag as the main sensing element, which increases the sensitivity of the antenna to the conductivity variation of the urine sample under the test as the result of dehydration. To accommodate older adult needs, this disposable tag can be embedded in a diaper as a wearable support or integrated with a catheter to monitor hydration in real-time. The fabricated sensor demonstrated a 7 dB decrease in resonant peak magnitude when the electrolyte concentration of the artificial urine sample changed from 2.5% (hydrated) to 5.0% (dehydrated).

articleTitle: Detection of Prairie Grassland Mowing Using Polarimetric Microwave Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Remote sensing methods have historically been used to monitor grassland vegetation height as changes may be accompanied by negative environmental impacts. Previous studies analyzed the suitability of satellites for monitoring grassland mowing and grazing events, but there is limited knowledge of the usability of ground-based systems for this purpose. The goal of this study was to determine if C- and L-band ground based scatterometers could be used to detect and quantify changes in grass height. We compared the normalized radar cross sections (NRCS) of C- and L-band scatterometers before and after a grassland mowing event. Co-polarized (VV, HH) and cross-polarized signals were analyzed at the elevation angles of 30° and 55° for both scatterometer systems. Results showed as much as 5.1 dB decrease in backscatter for C-band occurred after the mowing event. The decrease at L-band was less significant (2.4 dB at most). The results of this study confirmed that ground-based scatterometer systems operating in C- and L-band can be used to detect mowing events.

articleTitle: Near Field Measurement: Characterizing System SNR Against Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: For estimating a far-field (FF) pattern, near-field (NF) measurement system manufacturers normally specify an expected accuracy for the peak gain, but seldom address the accuracy of the rest of the pattern. Many factors affect measurement accuracy, including the primary measurement parameter, signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR). To help understand the measurement system accuracy, a test procedure to quantify the SNR against the measurement frequency is discussed here. In a NF system, an automated vector network analyzer (VNA) is commonly used to estimate the path gain between the testing probe antenna and the antenna-under-test (AUT), for each NF spatial sample point and measurement frequency. While path gain measurement is founded on the deterministic Friis equation, for NF measurements, the FF gains require correction for good accuracy, and this is normally part of the calibration process. The SNR, and therefore the estimation accuracy, decreases for increasing frequencies, with cable attenuation dominating the losses as the frequencies reach the popular mmWave bands. Characterizing a system's SNR involves understanding the role of all the losses including the often-cryptic actions of the automated VNA.

articleTitle: Investigation of Flexible PCB-Based Ring Array of Slots Using Phase-Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: An investigation into the feasibility of a flexible printed circuit board ring array of slot antennas is presented. The goal is to design an easy-to-manufacture antenna for scanning a beam in azimuth using phase-mode excitation. The basic formulation includes a new and illuminating modification to the matrix-based formulation for phase-mode excitation. From simulation, the antenna concept has broadband performance, although reducing the back-lobe calls for further research.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Shared Aperture Antenna Using Sequentially Rotated Elements for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A Right Hand Circularly Polarized (RHCP) Shared Aperture Antenna (SAA) is proposed which has a 2 × 2 sequentially rotated array of X-band patches in a square-ring antenna with crossed strips operating in the GPS band. The array has enhanced Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth, beamwidth and RHCP gain compared to those of single X-band patch antenna inside the SAA. The array exhibits a 62% increase in AR bandwidth. The AR beamwidth increases to 30° and 36° from 10° and 13° of single X-band patch antenna in the E- and H-planes, respectively. The array also improves the RCHP gain to 13.8 dBic from 11.7 dBic with only one patch antenna and restores the peak gain to boresight. The overall dimension of 65 × 65 × 18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> makes the proposed array SAA a compact, wideband, high gain antenna for applications in high-speed CubeSat communications.

articleTitle: Parametric 3D Full Wave EM Study for Designing Optimized Phase-Change RF Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper focuses on using a 3D full wave EM field solver to accurately modeling and predicting the radio frequency (RF) performance by coupling thermal characteristics of the phase-change material and optimizing various design dimensions. A fabricated RF switch is demonstrated with the performance matching closely with the full-wave 3D EM model. An optimal RF performance is achieved through accurate design and careful characterization of the micro-fabrication process. Parametric studies are carried out on a phase-change series single-pole single-throw switch model. The switch is designed with conformal coverage of the materials to represent actual fabricated device. In EM modeling, the material properties were taken by experimentally extracting various characteristics including but not limited to conductivity, sheet resistance, melting point, thermal expansion, stresses to name a few.

articleTitle: An Electrodynamics Solver for Moving Sources
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: An Electrodynamics solver for moving sources is introduced. The main challenges and formulation are highlighted. The solver enables the simulation of fields for sources undergoing arbitrary motion. Two examples of uniformly moving current sources are provided to correlate the numerical solver computations with theory, based on the solution of Maxwell's equations and the relativistic transformation of the electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: VO2-Based Reconfigurable Electromagnetic Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present an overview of our group's work with vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) as a novel material for reconfigurable mmWave electromagnetic (EM) surfaces and devices. VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is a phase change material (PCM) that experiences a metal-insulator transition (MIT) at 68°C. We first present our prior work with reflectarrays and VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> for mmWave applications. We then present a detailed discussion of the design and test setup for a VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based reconfigurable linear-to-circular polarization (LCP) converter metasurface operating in the Ka uplink band (27.5-31 GHz). The LCP converter can be reconfigured to output left-handed or right-handed circular polarization using VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switches. A quasi-optical free-space measurement setup is used for characterizing the device. Preliminary measurement results correlate well with simulations. Phase error, axial ratio, and insertion loss are below 20°, 3 dB, and 1 dB, respectively, across the Ka uplink band for a static, non-reconfigurable device.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of A RFSoC FPGA-Based Single-Chip Digital-RF Radio
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a new all-digital transceiver fully implemented on a single radio-frequency system-on-chip (RF-SoC) field-programmable gate array (FPGA) chip. Both the radio frequency (RF) transmitter and receiver were entirely implemented in a single reconfigurable chip. The transceiver provides agility and flexibility in terms of carrier frequency, bandwidth, and modulation capabilities. A hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbench setup was used to evaluate the transceiver's performance. Error-vector magnitude (EVM) and bit error rate (BER) figures of merit were used to evaluate the signal quality. This architecture assists in reducing size, weight, power and cost (SWaP-C) requirements since no JESD204 IP interface protocol is used to connect the FPGA to the data converters. To the best of the author's knowledge, this is the first RF-SoC FPGA-based digital-RF transceiver realization capable of directly generating RF signals for the sub-6 GHz frequencies. The proposed design enables the implementation of an all-digital RF transmitter using FPGAs.

articleTitle: On Multiple-Resonance Scattering Modes of a Circular Dielectric Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of scattering of an E-polarized electromagnetic wave on a homogeneous dielectric cylinder with a circular cross section is investigated. On the basis of explicit representations of the scattered-field expansion coefficients and using the implicit function theorem in the complex domain, the Cauchy problems are formulated and solved to find the curves determining the modes of resonance scattering. Particularly, the modes of double and triple mutiple-resonance scattering are found and described.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Integrated Fabry–Perot Cavity
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, a new dielectric resonator antenna is introduced for 5G wireless communication systems at mm-wave bands. The proposed antenna consists of a cylinder dielectric resonator with an integrated Fabry-Perot cavity and is fed using an L-probe to match its characteristic impedance. The antenna is designed so that high efficiency and gain are simultaneously achieved. Using this, approach, the obtained results show an impedance bandwidth of 56.4%, ranging from 25.9 GHz to 46.2 GHz. The antenna provides a peak realized gain of 10.3 dBi at 30 GHz and radiation efficiency of 95% across the entire operating band. The antenna radiation patterns in both the E- and H-planes are stable across the entire operating band, making it a good candidate for 5G applications at mm-wave bands.

articleTitle: Some Possibilities for Utilizing Metasurfaces in Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper reviews some of our recent works on how electromagnetic metasurfaces could be advantageously used for microwave imaging applications. In particular, it discusses some possibilities for augmenting the information content of the data and enhancing the achievable signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Hybrid DRA With Hexagonal Substrate for W-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Millimeter wave frequency band is the most innovative field that provides wide bandwidth for various security and medical applications. The paper presents an ultra-wide band hybrid dielectric resonator antenna for the range of 86.9 GHz-120 GHz. It provides a reasonable gain of 6.74 dBi and 6.2 dBi exhibiting 84.8% and 80.7% radiating efficiency at the frequencies of 94 GHz and 110 GHz. The proposed structure can be used for passive and active imaging applications where ultra-wide bandwidth is required and can be a good candidate for security and surveillance applications.

articleTitle: Transformation of Chiral and Tellegen Nihility
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Bi-isotropic media are known in theory of wave-matter interactions at least for a century. An exotic case of such interactions occurs if the corresponding permittivity and permeability vanish while one of the magnetoelectric coupling coefficients is not zero. In this paper, we discuss these alluring media called chiral and Tellegen nihility. Particularly, we show that by using generalized duality transformation, it is possible to transform only Tellegen nihility into a magnetodielectric medium, whose permittivity and permeability have specific values. Also, we briefly elucidate properties of plane waves in those media and indicate that in contrast to chiral nihility, the eigenfields in Tellegen nihility have different handedness resulting in zero averaged power density. This enticing conclusion is confirmed by studies of the transformed magnetodielectric medium. We hope that our work helps especially to realize Tellegen nihility media effects which is difficult in practice.

articleTitle: Transfer Matrix Method of Modulation-Based Space-Time Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Amidst the current renewal of interest for space-time modulated structures, there is a need for simple modeling tools. In this context, the transfer-matrix method (TMM) has recently been generalized to space-time structures. The derivation of this generalized TMM requires acrobatic frame-hopping, and the resulting equations lack symmetry. Here, we present an alternative derivation that avoids frame-hopping and treats the temporal and the spatial periodicities in a symmetric fashion. This leads to simpler equations with easier interpretation.

articleTitle: On Effects of Varying SINR for Source Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Source detection is an important problem in array signal processing. Many different deep learning based models have been proposed to estimate the number of sources which have outperformed conventional methods. These solutions have been promising in scenarios with low SINR (Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio), small number of snapshots, and large number of sources. However these models are trained on a constant value of SINR. Here we investigate if deep learning based approaches can perform source detection on a wide range of SINRs.

articleTitle: Volatile Organic Compound Wireless Monitoring at a Low-Profile and Passive Resonant Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The Development of microwave gas sensors with a low-profile design and enhanced sensitivity is a continuing challenge. This summary describes the wireless detection of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) by a resonant surface integrated with a thin (0.08 mm) polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) dielectric interface. Resonating at ~8.5 GHz, the surface was mounted on an RT5880 Rogers substrate with a thickness of 0.51mm, backed up by a ground plane. Upon the presence of VOCs, the PDMS layer started interacting with the vapor molecules and swelled. The swelling affected the effective permittivity of the SRR's topside medium, subsequently changing the resonant frequency. The variations in the SRR's resonant characteristics were monitored using a bi-static configuration of horn antennas. Experimental results indicated that for 1–3 milliliters of tetrahydrofuran (THF) in the chamber, the sensor demonstrated a 140 MHz in the resonant frequency. With a low-profile and passive design, this microwave gas sensor enables the wireless detection of VOCs in applications where cabling and power requirements, and accessibility are limiting concerns.

articleTitle: Detection of 532nm Laser Light Using a TiO2 Nanotube Integrated Microwave Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Optical sensors play an important role in applications of the biomedical industry and in monitoring potentially hazardous gases. This paper presents an integration of TiO2 nanotube (TNT) membranes coated on a microwave split ring resonator (SRR) to detect a 532 nm laser light. A SRR was designed with integrated TNT membranes at an operational frequency of 8.006 GHz with a resonant notch amplitude of −11.4 dB. The illumination of TiO2 changed the dielectric properties (optical properties of the TiO2) of the material, and this variation was monitored through the transmission coefficient S21. The designed integrated microwave resonator achieved a resonant amplitude change of 0.6 dB with a 6 MHz frequency downshift in a duration of 10 seconds of 532 nm laser exposure. The laser operated at a power of 5 mW and was located at a distance of 30 cm above the target resonator. The proposed design is the first exploration of the integration of TNT membranes with a microwave resonator for pioneering new forms of optical sensors.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Modeling of UWB Antennas for GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A deep neural network (DNN) is developed for predicting the performance of a miniaturized lightweight highgain ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna. The DNN models the reflection coefficient and gain in terms of the input design parameters of the antenna. For comparison, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) is also investigated. The DNN model is found to outperform the MLP model.

articleTitle: Perforated 3D Printed Short Backfire Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A design for a short backfire antenna is presented that reduces the weight of the antenna while maintaining the performance by introducing perforations in the antenna and fabricating it with a lightweight material using a 3D printing technique. Parametric studies were done to investigate the effects of the perforations on the antenna and the optimal performance was obtained. The weight of the 3D printed perforated SBF antenna is calculated to be about 20% of the original aluminum design (80% reduction in mass).

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Optical Coupling in Frustrated Total Internal Reflection (FTIR) Using Maxwell's Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Frustrated total internal reflection (FTIR) is an intriguing phenomenon which surfaced when evanescent waves were observed while experimentally studying the total internal reflection (TIR). This paper presents a theoretical analysis and numerical results of the phenomenon of frustrated total internal reflection (FTIR) based on Maxwell's equations. This is the oldest form of tunneling discovered in physics, which was later considered analogous to quantum tunneling, mainly because the physics of tunneling is essentially identical for classical light waves and quantum mechanical wave functions. This phenomenon has several practical implications like fingerprint sensing, laser cavity design, and studying the physics and chemistry of optically transparent semiconductors.

articleTitle: Wearable Chipless Antenna Sensors as Smart Bandages
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a system for real-time monitoring of chronic wounds. The proposed printed chipless antenna-based sensor adopted spiral resonators to assess the key parameters in chronic wounds including their pH level, temperature, and irregular bleeding. The captured physiological data will then go through a nearby reader to investigate the wound situation and demonstrate whether it is healing or not. This system is light weight, low-cost and environmentally friendly as it does not possess batteries and will be fabricated by additive manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Interpretation and Separability of the Effective Permittivity in Case that Both Permittivity and Conductivity are Complex
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper is about the interpretation and separability of the effective permittivity in case that both the permittivity and the conductivity are dispersive and thus complex-valued. It is shown that: a) it is always possible to retrieve the static conductivity and the high-frequency (optical) permittivity from the effective permittivity; b) it is in general not possible to separate the complex conductivity from the complex permittivity. The findings rely on the application of the Hilbert transform and their effectiveness is verified by means of a numerical example.

articleTitle: Dual Band Shared Aperture Antenna for 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This work presents design of a dual band antenna for the 5G communications in the millimeter wave band. As opposed to conventional patch antennas which are limited to single narrow band operation a shared aperture concept is utilized for this antenna. The patch aperture is coupled through two rectangular slots etched on a thin printed circuit board (100μm). The patch is elevated in air thus avoiding excitation of surface waves and minimizing dielectric losses at millimeter wave frequencies. With this approach the radiator can cover lower band of 28 GHz and upper band of 37/ 39 GHz dedicated for the fifth generation communications. The simulated radiation efficiency of the antenna stays above 90%.

articleTitle: Radar Fusion for Enhanced Driver Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Human respiratory patterns, as manifested through chest and abdominal breathing, can provide insight into both physical and mental states, and can be monitored in order to detect and prevent health issues during driving. Non-contact sensors are preferred for long-term monitoring due to their convenience, and among non-contact techniques, radar has been shown to accurately estimate breathing patterns while preserving privacy, making it a popular choice for driver status monitoring. One potential breathing concern is shortness of breath, which can be difficult to detect using a single monitoring location. In the proposed method, a fusion of two 60 GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars to accurately recognize shortness of breath in drivers is used and demonstrated through experimental results that this fusion is able to eliminate false detections.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Antennas' Design Criteria and Measurement Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The contrast between the design criteria for electrically small transmit and receive antennas is studied in this work. On the transmit side, radiation efficiency (ohmic loss plus return loss) and data throughput are critical. However, a higher impedance mismatch on the receiving front end may reduce ohmic loss and expand the frequency bandwidth. So, a calculated mismatch can be added to improve the performance of the receiving ESA by lowering the overall noise figure and widening the frequency bandwidth. These contradictory design criteria suggest utilizing separate transmit and receive antennas to improve the transmitter and receiver performances.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna with Surface-Mounted Grooved Horn Using PRGW for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The paper presents a high gain, wide-band, dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna with a surface mounted horn for mm-wave applications using printed ridge-gap waveguide technology. At the center frequency 30 GHz, the proposed antenna achieves a 20% relative impedance bandwidth for the frequency range from 27 GHz to 33 GHz. The antenna gain has been enhanced using a grooved horn. The ME dipole antenna achieved a gain level of 16 ± 0.7 dBi over the operating band. With this large bandwidth and gain, this antenna configuration using PRGW technology is suitable for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: Packaged Sub-array Overlapping Feeding Network for mmWave
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: AMC packaged Multi-layer overlapped sub-array has been investigated for mmWave application for the first time. The design of the array has been based on the roots of transfer functions of sub-arrays. The structures are implemented in multiple layers to realize complex sub-array overlapping with a smaller number of crossovers. Besides, the AMC packaging is utilized to suppress the spurious radiation from microstrip lines at mm frequency. The Full-wave results are acceptably compatible with design computations.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave (MM-Wave) Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) with 20:1 Bandwidth and 45° Volumetric Scanning
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband (UWB) array is presented, operating from L- band to 40 GHz. The novelty of this design is the simplification of the fabrication by utilizing a hybrid approach that uses i) very low-loss Rogers substrate for the fabrication of the antenna elements with its double- Y balun feed, ii) a 3D structure fabrication for high precision assembly. Design simulation showed a VSWR < 2.8 at broadside and scanning down to 45° in all planes across the 2 – 40 GHz band. These simulations will be validated through fabrication and measurement of a 15 × 15 array prototype, to be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Simulating C-Band Radar Backscatter of Oil-Covered New Ice in a Mesocosm
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present model results for C-band radar backscatter response from oil-covered new ice in a mesocosm with oil layer thicknesses between 0 and 5 cm. We used the first-order approximation of small perturbation method (SPM) to account for multilayered surface scattering from the air–oil, oil–ice, and icewater interfaces. To relate the scattering to the new ice surface dielectric, we employed simulated radar data to derive a copolarization ratio parameter that weakens the effect of surface roughness in the SPM model. Our findings provide the physical basis for inverting oil thickness and suggest that such inversion may be possible from current and future radar satellites during freeze-up seasons.

articleTitle: Contaminants Detection in Industrial Products Through Microwave Imaging and Compressive Sensing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Microwave technology has bee recently proposed as an innovative and safe tool for in-line food quality control aimed at the detection and imaging of possible contaminants in packaged food products. The main challenges related to this application of microwave imaging is represented by the required high resolution, for the detection of very small contaminant, and the short time window available for measuring data, dictated by the speed of the production line. In particular, this latter constraint allows to gather only a reduced number of data. In such a framework, this contribution investigate the capabilities of a compressive sensing based imaging algorithm to retrieve accurate and high resolution images despite the low number of available measurements.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis for the Design of a Miniaturized FSS-Based Polarization Insensitive Transmission Rotator
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A novel systematic design procedure for the design of a transmission type linearly polarized (LP) polarization rotator is presented. The design approach exploits the CMA scattered fields for identifying the most promising FSS unit cell. A miniaturized frequency selective surface (FSS) unit call capable to support a pair of degenerate modes radiating a circularly polarized (CP) radiated field is proposed to obtain an efficient polarization rotator. The good agreement between simulated and measured results validates the benefits of adopting the CMA during the design as well as the remarkable performance.

articleTitle: Corrugated Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Enhanced Gain and Low-Mutual Coupling for High-Speed Wireless MIMO Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We propose a circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna fed by a printed ridge gap waveguide inverted microstrip line, the antenna achieves a 13.2-dBi peak gain. The radiation characteristics of the proposed antenna are improved significantly by the use of a dielectric ring. The antenna is employed in a rotated sequentially fed 2×2 antenna array configuration with a double superstrate, as such the individual element gain goes up to 16 dBi, and the sequentially rotated fed array gain goes up to 21.6 dBi.

articleTitle: The Effect of a Finite Circular Groundplane on Monopole Impedance
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The monopole on a circular groundplane is suitable as a benchmark for antenna analysis techniques. This is because its feed is a well-defined coaxial port which can be reasonably matched, and because its symmetrical structure allows a theoretical analysis although this is convenient only for when the monopole is impracticably thin. Any such thin-wire antenna has challenges for simulation because of the associated wide dynamic range of dimensions, but simulation can readily solve for practical monopole thicknesses. We present preliminary results from simulation and physical experiment for the feed-point resistance of a quarter wavelength monopole, noting that an electrically large groundplane allows this resistance to be related to a dipole. We also include simulation results for using a square ground-plane, which is easier to manufacture than the circular ground- plane.

articleTitle: A Multi-Frequency Suite of Polarimetric Scatterometers for Arctic Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present a suite of polarimetric microwave scatterometers for Arctic remote sensing applications. The systems have been developed with L- (1.26 GHz), C- (5.5 GHz), and Ku- (17.2 GHz) band designs. The instruments were designed for near-surface operation and can be used to measure the normalized radar cross section in linear polarizations (VV, HH, and VH), as well as polarimetric parameters. The units use a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) signal with pulse-to-pulse polarization switching. A mechanical positioner is used to orient the system to scan a region of interest. Herein, we describe the system technical parameters and the calibration routines. We provide sample data over a typical sea ice surface and describe system configurations. These systems are designed to provide multi-frequency polarimetric scattering data that can be analyzed for a wide variety of experiments in snow-covered sea ice and in Arctic oil spill studies.

articleTitle: Low-Loss 2-Bit Reflective Intelligent Surface for MM-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, a low-loss 2-bit Reflective Intelligent Surface (RIS) is proposed, as a digitally controlled system for electromagnetic beam manipulation, namely beam-steering. The full structure is composed of 225 independently tunable meta-atoms, using varactor diodes, providing 4 distinct phase states of 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees, binary coded as: “00”, “01”, “10”, and “11”, respectively. CST Microwave Studio is used for both the unit cell and full structure analysis, where a standard horn antenna is used to illuminate the programmable metasurface. The far-field beam-steering mechanism of the proposed antenna is achieved by digitally coding the RIS elements with unique coding sequences, to redirect the beam to a predefined angle. Simulation results show that the beam scanning range covers 60 degrees (±30), and this capability can be further extended to enable wider beam scanning, making the proposed programmable metasurface a potential candidate for future mm-wave wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A PEDOT:PSS and DC Line Enhanced Planar Microwave Humidity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Microwave sensors in the form of Split Ring Resonators are being utilized in an abundance of applications yet require constant advancements to maintain this course. This paper investigates the integration of an organic conductive polymer, PEDOT:PSS, with a planar microwave split ring resonator for humidity detection. A double gap split ring resonator was designed with quarter wavelength lines and radial stubs for the purpose of measuring the resistance of materials placed across the sensitive gap. A set of gold electrodes were sputtered on a thin glass slide, which was then spin coated with a thin film of PEDOT:PSS and bonded across the sensitive gap using a silver epoxy. Environmental variations in relative humidity affect the conductivity of the thin film, producing shifts in resonant amplitude, resonant frequency, and resistance. The sensor functionality was verified by varying humidity from 0 %RH to 75 %RH in an enclosed chamber for five cycles, producing 196.1 MHz, 1.131 dB, and 30.65 kΩ shifts in resonant frequency, resonant amplitude, and DC resistance respectively. Thus, the design not only demonstrates potential for humidity sensing, but establishes that investigating the interaction of microwaves and DC variations in materials is the next step in advancing microwave sensing devices.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Convoluted Frequency-Selective Surface with Single- and Dual-Band Response
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an RFSS based on slotted square with convoluted arms geometry, for 5G applications. The RFSS presents single- and dual-band response for the TM and TE polarization respectively. In the TM polarization, the diodes state switching does not change the RFSS response. For the TE polarization, the resonant frequencies change their values while switching the diodes' states. Simulated and measured results show to have a good agreement.

articleTitle: All-Metal Metasurface Antenna for W-Band Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: All metal metasurface antennas are under development for W-band radiometer at the NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. The metasurface antenna directs the radiated beam by the holographic approach. The pillbox beamformer is fed using one (or more) horns located at the focal plane of the parabolic reflector of the pillbox beamformer. These antennas are planar and low-profile and are thus suitable for Cubesat and Smallsat platforms. The proposed antenna demonstrates a directivity as high as 31 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 65%, and a reflection coefficient better than -15 dB in the desired 93-95 GHz frequency band. The antenna is being manufactured and the measured performance will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: A Transmisson Line Approach to Reduce Transition Sensitivity of a Filter Package on High Density PCB
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A transmission line based approach to improve transition sensitivity of filter packages on a high density printed circuit board (PCB) is proposed. It is useful for optimization and analysis of high frequency components on a substrate throughout design and simulation stages of a microwave system. For validation of the approach, a compact surface-mount filter package with very high rejection band is simulated and analyzed on a PCB. The concept of the work is simple yet an interesting RF design technique, which can enhance or maintain the performance of filters in desired frequency bands. Although the approach is applied to a particular component for demonstration, it can streamline the selection of various commercial discrete filters.

articleTitle: Wideband Planar Leaky-Wave Antenna Based on Grounded Coplanar Waveguide (GCPW) for Millimeter-Wave Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The well-known power/energy leakage phenomenon between an unshielded grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) and its neighboring parallel-plate waveguide (PPW) is artfully exploited herein to develop a class of leaky-wave antenna (LWAs), i.e., GCPW LWAs. Considering that both the GCPW and PPW behave in a non-dispersive manner regarding their dominant modes (i.e., quasi-TEM and TEM, respectively), the relevant angle of power leakage between them is kept constant, thereby paving the way for realizing a GCPW LWA radiating a wideband and fixed beam. To make the beam angle flexibly tailorable, three engineering approaches are proposed. Thanks to the merits of simple configuration, single layer, low cost, wideband radiation, and beam angle design flexibility, our proposed GCPW LWAs have potential applications in millimeter-wave wireless systems such as 60 GHz point-to-point communications.

articleTitle: A Metal Crack Sensor Based on Chipless RFID Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, a single patch sensor based on chipless Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology is proposed to detect the angle and width of metal cracks in engineering structures. The sensor is composed of a single polygon patch, which can save frequency band resources and improve the sensitivity of the sensor. The sensor is designed to operate in the frequency range of 3.4-5.5 GHz. The results show that the sensor can accurately identify cracks at all angles and widths. The sensitivity of the sensor reaches 12.74 MHz/0.1mm. Moreover, high sensitivity and good reliability are achieved by adopting passive design.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Sparse Array Design for Fast Antenna Switching in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Reconfigurable sparse antennas arrays are emerging to be an integral part of cognitive sensing in dynamic radio frequency (RF) environments. Fast-switching is, therefore, instrumental to a realizable perception-action cycle. In this paper, we design sparse arrays using binary switching per RF chain achieving optimum beamforming that maximizes the signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (SINR) over an angular sector containing the desired source direction. We apply two binary switching strategies and design the respective optimal array configuration common to the angular sector of interest using convolutional neural networks. We examine the performance of the proposed scheme in terms of the achievable sparse array classification rates and SINR.

articleTitle: Vertical Ground Electrode Fault Detection Using Surface Wave Time Domain Reflectometry (SW-TDR) Excited with a Horn Launcher
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A grounding network is an integral part of an electrical power substation. It protects expensive equipment and provides safety to workers. This paper presents a Surface Wave (SW) Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) technique for grounding network health integrity monitoring by detecting faults in vertical grounding electrodes. In SW-TDR, a fast rise-time pulse is applied using a horn launcher into the grounding electrode. The injected pulse travels along the electrode in the form of a transverse magnetic (TM) propagating mode and is reflected at any impedance mismatch, such as a break-point in the electrode. By investigating the reflected signal waveform, the mismatch location and severity can be identified. Theoretical expressions and simulation of the fields of the surface wave guided by a single electrode in a lossy media is presented. A single electrode system with a conical horn launcher is designed and analyzed using full wave electromagnetic simulation to evaluate the wide-band input impedance and then TDR response as obtained by applying FFT. The results show that the SW-TDR is capable of detecting break-points in a grounding electrode for a system bandwidth of 300 MHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Inversion for Metasurface Design-A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper reviews some of our recent research progress in the area of electromagnetic inverse metasurface design. In particular, the scope of this paper is on the inverse design of omega-bianisotropic transmitting metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Evolutionary Optimization Methods for Electromagnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Metalens design and fabrication in the optical regime presents many exciting opportunities for developing state-of-the-art optics technologies. However, fabricating electrically large devices at scale for optical wavelengths is a major challenge due to limits in existing lithographic fabrication techniques. In this summary, we present our work for counteracting performance losses arising from geometric uncertainty of fabricated devices (e.g., metasurface supercells). We employed Deep Learning (DL) methods to overcome the inherent intractability of exhaustive robustness testing, and a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm was used to find tolerant yet efficient device designs. When amortized over several optimization runs, the proposed DL-augmented optimization scheme offers a speedup of more than 10 times over a full-wave-only strategy.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Ground Beef for Microwave Sensing and Imaging Phantoms: Measurement Considerations and Effect of Dehydration
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Ground meat may be used to mimic the dielectric properties of human tissue when validating microwave sensors and algorithms. Accurate measurements of the dielectric properties of ground meat are important for this validation. Based on a pilot study, key considerations for taking reliable measurements of ground beef samples and the effect of hydration on ground beef properties are reported.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Engineering Using Time-Varying Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Passive, linear and time-invariant resonators suffer from limited bandwidth, and size miniaturization leads to still narrower operational bandwidth. Leveraging time-varying circuit elements is one solution to overcome such limitations. Here, we utilize slow time modulation of resistive elements to engineer and enhance a resonator's bandwidth, emulating resonant response at multiple frequencies simultaneously. We experimentally verify the proposed technique, demonstrating the enhancement of radiation of a broadband modulated signal radiated by planar inverted-F antenna.

articleTitle: Coated Metasurfaces for Decoupling and Cloaking of Rectangular Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we apply the concept of electromagnetic cloaking in order to reduce the mutual coupling between two rectangular patch antennas placed very close to each other (sub-wavelength separation). In particular, we show that by coating the top surfaces of the patch antennas with suitably patterned metasurfaces, it is possible to make each patch antenna electromagnetically invisible to the other antenna. Along with this, it is also shown that the individual radiation characteristics of each antenna is restored, as if they were isolated. The decoupling and cloaking action of the metasurfaces are demonstrated by various full-wave numerical simulation results. The novelty of our design lies in the fact that these specific metasurfaces accomplish cloaking of an electrically large surface (length equal to half of the wavelength within dielectric medium).

articleTitle: PEDOT:PSS Integrated Resonant Absorbing Surface for an Antenna-Based Humidity Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Monitoring environmental humidity at microwave frequencies has attracted significant interest in agricultural and biomedical applications. This work investigates the integration of PEDOT:PSS material with a periodic resonant structure as a humidity sensor. The proposed periodic structure comprises an array of 6 × 4 unit cells fabricated on a low-cost FR-4 substrate with an overall dimension of 120 mmx80 mmx1.57 mm. Exposing the sensor to the humidity alters the complex permittivity of the PEDOT:PSS material and consequently reduces the resonant frequency and magnitude of the structure. An interrogating horn antenna communicates with the proposed sensor at a distance of 20 cm to track the changes in the resonant profile wirelessly. At 4% relative humidity level, the proposed sensor provides an absorption peak at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\mathrm{r}}=2.283$</tex> GHz with a magnitude of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{\mathrm{r}}=-{4}4$</tex> dB. Increasing the humidity level to 64%, changes the resonant frequency and amplitude with the magnitude of -36.5 MHz and 8 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Broadband Circularly-Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband circularly-polarized (CP) sequential-fed dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications. The proposed antenna array has a wide 10-dB bandwidth of 4.36 GHz (24.89-29.25 GHz) and peak gain of more than 7.28 dBi within the operating band. The broadband response is achieved by placing a ring-shaped DRA over the cylindrical one. In this work, a sequential feeding network along with Z-shaped slots beneath the DRAs is used to achieve CP operation in a 2×2 array. It exhibits a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 1.87 GHz (26.5-28.37 GHz). Moreover, it has a total efficiency and radiation efficiency of 80.14% and 95.83%, respectively. Due to its broadband operation range, wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth, high gain and efficiency, this antenna array is suitable choice for mm-wave wireless communication devices.

articleTitle: Switching Bianisotropic Media
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Temporal discontinuities of effective parameters of materials have recently received significant attention since they result in novel wave phenomena. However, the literature has been primarily contemplating sudden changes of permittivity tensors corresponding to dielectrics, plasmas, magnetized plasmas, etc. In this talk, we extend this crucial study to bianisotropic media, and, particularly, we report our recent results about switching the electromagnetic coupling in reciprocal chiral and omega media. We show that, for example, how fast switching of the coupling coefficient allows us to create a spin-dependent or directional-dependent response. We also describe the effect of temporal discontinuities in nonreciprocal bianisotropic media, i.e., Tellegen and moving media. We hope that our talk provides a comprehensive perspective on switched bianisotropic media and paves the road for future research in this emerging area.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Far-Field Pattern of an X-Band Electronically Controlled Reflectarray Antenna Assisted by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we use neural network (NN) machine learning (ML) to optimize the far field (FF) radiation pattern of an electronically reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (ERRA). ML enables us to predict the voltage set to apply on the unit cells of the ERRA to orient the main lobe in a desired direction and lower the sidelobe level.

articleTitle: 9th Order Cavity Filter Design and Optimization Utilizing AI Method of Synmatrix Software
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we present a design procedure of a 9th-order bandpass cavity filter at 2.655GHz with three transmission zeros using Artificial Intelligence Tuning of the Synmatrix software. After 28 iterations, the initial frequency error level of 60% decreased to 3%, while the initial coupling error of 27% declined to 1%. The designed fabricated filter was measured, and the measurement and simulation results were in good agreement.

articleTitle: Dual Membrane Multiport DC-40 GHz RF Microelectromechanical Switches
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This article reports unique dual membrane multi-port DC-40 GHz radio frequency (RF) microelectromechanical switches. A single-pole double-throw (SPDT) design is presented with a metal-to-metal contact switch in series with a capacitive membrane to achieve better isolation performance over the entire operational range. The switches are fabricated using a seven-layer UWMEMS microfabrication process on alumina substrate and the electromagnetic modeling of the switches is discussed in detail. Full field 3D model is developed to include conformal thin-film discontinuities and the material database for the simulations are characterized and extracted experimentally. At 20 GHz, the presented switch topology demonstrate better than 0.35 dB of insertion loss and higher than 40 dB isolation performance.

articleTitle: Intelligent Ice Detection Based on Artificial Neural Network Using Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Microwave-based material detection involves vector network analyzer measurements with high frequency sweep points (e.g.,> 1000), which increases the cost of subsequent data processing. When implementing artificial intelligence (AI) on a chip for data processing, a large number of frequency sweep points increases the size of the neural network which adds significant power and area overheads. This work presents a machine learning (ML) model using an artificial neural network architecture for detecting ice, water, and air by only using four frequency points. At the core, the sensing of material and the collection of datasets are based on the response of a microwave SRR sensor. This microwave resonator is designed to operate at 5.1 GHz, enabling the sensing of ice, water, and air based on the permittivity and thickness variations. After the proper selection of four frequency points based on the change of the resonator's characteristics over a narrow frequency range of 4.6 GHz to 5.2 GHz, the ML model is trained and tested using gradient descent with the backpropagation method. The ML model achieves a high inference accuracy of 98.8%. This development based on a microwave resonator sensor and AI-chip provides a practical solution for ice detection applications, where lowering the cost in terms of power consumption and device implementation are the major criteria.

articleTitle: Near-Field Sensing Improvement of a Radar AntennaOn-Chip Using a Transmissive Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The design of a planar transmissive superstrate for near-field sensing improvement of the compact short-range radar antenna is presented. The superstrate structure is designed to be placed at a half wavelength above the radar transmitter/receiver antennas while contacting human skin without airgap. The purpose is to increase the power absorbed from the transmitter antenna into the human skin while simultaneously improving the radar SNR. The proposed superstrate with dimensions of 1.54 λ × 1.54 λ × 0.16 λ consists of two metallic layers of a phase-corrected microstrip crossed-dipole array printed on both sides of a substrate. Using full-wave electromagnetic simulations, the nearfield analysis inside the human skin model illustrates that using the planar superstrate enhances the near-field Poynting power into a human skin model from 19,825 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 41,585 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> which is a 2.1 times improvement, and the transmit-receive coupling analysis demonstrates an improvement of 5.2 dB of the radar received power.

articleTitle: Multiband Wearable Antenna for Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The use of wearable antenna is rising because of miniaturization in low power wireless devices. For multiband operation, the proposed design includes a U-shape and a horizontal slit at the patch and ground of the antenna. The antenna is designed and fabricated using single-layer Jeans and pure copper polyester taffeta fabric. For this, we achieved simulated bandwidths of 3.72% for 2.37 GHz to 2.46 GHz, 3.98% for 3.44 GHz to 3.58 GHz, and 0.77% for 5.76 GHz to 5.85 GHz, and Measured bandwidths are 10.75% for 2.2 GHz to 2.45 GHz, 5.68% for 3.42 GHz to 3.62 GHz and 5.65% for 5.67 GHz to 6 GHz. The first band is 2.42 GHz with the return loss of −17.73 dB magnitude, with the return loss of −18.9dB magnitude for the second band at 3.5 GHz, and the return loss of −11dB magnitude for the third band at 5.81 GHz was obtained through simulation, While the measured frequencies of 2.37 GHz, 3.47 GHz, and 5.82 GHz with return losses of correspondingly −15.18 dB magnitude, −12.95 dB magnitude, and −10.77 dB magnitude were obtained. The radiation performance is broadside in nature. The proposed wearable antenna can be used at ISM (2.4GHz and 5.8 GHz) and WiMAX (3.5 GHz) bands for energy harvesting applications.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Octave-Band Feed Horn Antenna for Radio Astronomy Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A novel multi step quad-ridged horn antenna (QRHA) with corrugations is demonstrated for operation over the 20 GHz to 40 GHz frequency range. The quad-ridged section is responsible for ensuring a wideband operation, whereas the corrugations support hybrid modes to obtain stable radiation patterns that taper to -16 dB at a half-angle beamwidth of 55° over the entire range. The multi-step profile improves efficiency by introducing higher order modes in the horn aperture, and shaping the sidewalls of the ridge horn contributes significantly to the radiation characteristics of the horns. To verify results, the horn is designed and simulated with both CST Microwave Studio and the μWaveWizard. Good agreement between the results of both software packages is observed which confirms the validity of this approach. The input reflection coefficient is mostly better than -20 dB over the entire frequency range, and an aperture efficiency of 75% to 80% is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Resonance Scattering and Cloaking: On a Unified Mathematical Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We develop a unified approach aimed at the determination of the quantities associated with resonance scattering and cloaking that employs complex mappings. The technique is a generalization of the method of dispersion curves and other similar versions of determining parameter dependence of the resonance and cloaking when only one real variable is varied, e.g. frequency. The approach is based on the obtained explicit expressions for the parameter sets for canonical structures having circular or planar symmetry at which resonance scattering or partial invisibility are achieved and when the scattered-field expansion coefficients are analyzed as functions of several complex variables. The approach is illustrated for the case of the simplest benchmark structure, the scatterer in the form of a homogeneous dielectric cylinder having circular cross-section.

articleTitle: Path Loss Measurements at 3455 MHz in Support of Localised Access to Midband Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: As spectrum become increasingly congested with new users, services and applications in the 5G mid-band, the coverage and interference estimates need to be more accurately predicted. This paper presents a preliminary analysis of path loss measurements on point-to-point links at 3455 MHz between 15 elevated antenna sites in the urban part of Ottawa, Canada. This data was used to validate the P.1812 propagation path loss model. Model predictions were shown to agree within 9 dB RMSE of measurements.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Linear Antennas Through Metasurface Coatings
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We review our recent results about the design of cylindrical metasurface coats for linear antennas enabling either frequency or radiation pattern reconfigurability. First, we show how, by a judicious tuning of the characteristics of a homogeneous metasurface coating, the resonant frequency of a dipole antenna can be shifted within a broad frequency range without modifying its length. Then, we explore the possibility enabled by inhomogeneous metasurfaces in shaping the antenna radiation pattern. The results may further boost the research toward the design of smart antennas and repeaters for next-generation communications.

articleTitle: Channel Characteristics Analysis for Joint-Cabin Scenario at Millimeter Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: To support the requirements for transmission and processing of the large amounts of data in the vision of “smart aviation”, millimeter wave communication for the fifth-generation (5G) wireless network has attracted great attention. However, the space in the aircraft is separated into small compartments. The 60 GHz has poor ability to penetrate the walls separating the compartments. Joint-cabin consists of two adjacent compartments with small hole on the wall. The joint-cabin will increase the utilization of the transmitter, and will also bring a new challenge on the accurate radio channel characterization for this scenario. In this paper, the joint-cabin contains a cargo compartment and an avionics compartment. Extensive ray-tracing (RT) simulation is performed to depict the radio propagation in the scenario. Channel characteristics for both cargo and avionics compartment are extracted based on the RT simulation, including root-meansquare delay spread (RMS DS) and power ratio (PR). Moreover, this paper proposes tapped-delay lines (TDL) model for the jointcabin scenario, of which the relative time delay, normalized power and fading distribution of each tap are analyzed. Our research outcomes will provide valuable insights into the system design and evaluation for the aircraft cabin.

articleTitle: Combined Microwave Inverse Source and Scattering Solution: High Contrast Targets in Near Field Zone
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this work, a phaseless solutions of inverse source and scattering problem is addressed. The combination of an inverse source strategy and of an inverse scattering method has been validated by considering a numerical near-field 3D scattering model, with the presence of high permittivity targets. The solution reveals the potentialities of microwaves inverse source/scattering without the use of any phase content.

articleTitle: Trade-Off Between Maximum Broadside Directivity and Scan Range of Small Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The primary performance parameters for a phased array are scan range and gain. They depend on both the array factor and the element pattern, with an increasingly directive element increasing the array directivity but decreasing the scan range. This trade-off is discussed in terms of the element spacing and the element directivity using a simple element pattern model. Many array results are from the classical model of separating the element and array factors but are not applicable to practical small arrays because the embedded element patterns can be different from each other. In terms of wideband design, there is an optimum element spacing for a linear array, for maximum scan range, maximum broadside gain, and array size (number of elements).

articleTitle: Coil Geometry Effects on the Efficiency of Wireless Power Transfer for Brain Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper a voxel brain model consisting of four different tissues is used to study the wireless power transfer for brain implants utilizing the inductive method. ANSYS Maxwell/Simplorer have been used for the simulation of the system. Coils with different geometries were designed, optimized, and then compared in terms of their power transfer efficiency. The effect of changing the position of the implanted coil, thus changing the distance between the coils on the coupling coefficient and power transfer efficiency was studied.

articleTitle: A Wideband Anisotropic Metasurface for Cross-polarization Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper presents a reflective metasurface demonstrating cross-polarization conversion (CPC). The proposed metasurface consists of T-shaped unit cells that are tilted at an angle of 45°, and each unit cell has two strips that are attached to a square located at its center. The proposed metasurface has the ability to convert a linearly-polarized wave into its orthogonal component across a broad range of frequencies, spanning from 8.06 GHz to 20.94 GHz, with a CPC efficiency of over 90%.

articleTitle: A Multistatic Imaging Algorithm Based on a Spatial Domain Decomposition Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A spatial domain decomposition approach in connection with a multistatic near-field imaging algorithm is analyzed. The multistatic scattering data is transformed into an equivalent monostatic representation. This is achieved by decomposing the imaging domain into subdomains and assigning a reference point to each of the individual subdomains, for which the multistatic-to-monostatic conversion is performed separately. The spatial image is computed for each subdomain individually and the final image is obtained by coherently superimposing the overlapping subimages using an appropriate spatial weighting. Multiple measurement results showcase the benefit of the spatial domain decomposition approach as well as its limitations.

articleTitle: Risley Prism with Integrated Phase Correcting Structure Excited by Circularly Polarized Patch Array with Enhanced Gain and Beam Steering Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper investigates beam steering response of a right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) 2 × 2 patch array with enhanced gain employing Risley prism (RP) concept with integrated parabolic phase correcting structure (PPCS) at 30 GHz. A pair of dielectric wedge-based RP elements are axially rotated in same or opposite direction to steer the incident beam in a conical space with an apex angle of 96°. A PPCS of 40 mm is integrated to the bottom dielectric wedge which enhances gain of the overall broadside and steered patterns by 5 dB. Realized gain of the broadside beam for the beam steering solution using the patch array at 30 GHz is 16.27 dBic. The impedance bandwidth, 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth and 3 dB gain bandwidth of the beam steering solution with the 2 × 2 patch array are better than 2 GHz.

articleTitle: Triple-Mode OAM Generating Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator (CDR) is proposed for generating triple-mode Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) carrying beams. More specifically, the OAM modes of 0, -1, and +1 can be excited using the single antenna element (CDR) according to different feed positions. Thus, the structure has three input ports, each one assigned for the one OAM mode. In order to make a mode-tunable structure, a feeding network including a Single Port Triple Through (SP3T) switch is utilized to alter the signal direction toward the specific feeding positions. The simulated results verify the generation of vortex beams with clockwise and anti-clockwise helical phase fronts for modes -1 and +1, respectively. The fundamental mode (mode 0) having a directive radiation pattern is excited as well. This structure, to the best of authors' knowledge, is the first reported single antenna element providing triple OAM modes with reconfigurable (mode-switchable structure) and non-reconfigurable (having individual port for each mode) capability.

articleTitle: An Inherently Broadband A - Φ Formulation Solver in Electromagnetics Based on Discrete Exterior Calculus
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: An efficient and inherently broadband numerical solver based on discrete exterior calculus (DEC) for the A-Φ formulation in electromagnetics is proposed. The A-Φ formulation with generalized Lorenz gauge is immune to low-frequency breakdown, which makes the proposed solver ideal for broadband and multi-scale analysis. DEC is utilized as the numerical solver to the A-Φ formulation, where Stokes' theorem and charge conservation are naturally preserved. In addition, DEC can be viewed as a generalized version of finite difference method with unstructured mesh, such as tetrahedral mesh. Thus, complicated multi-scale structures can be discretized easily and efficiently by DEC. Numerical results are presented which indicate the broadband stable nature of the proposed A-Φ DEC solver over an extremely wide bandwidth (from DC to optics).

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithm for Recognition of Neurological Disorders Using a Multichannel Battery-Free Wireless Brain Implant Recorder
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Automatic monitoring of neural activity can lead to the recognition of neurological patient disorders in real time. In this study, we present an evaluation of a multichannel, battery-free, and fully implantable wireless neurosensing system (WiNS). Signal quality from WiNS is compared with a commercially available wired system employing machine learning algorithms. Somatosensory evoked potential from fore limb and Whisker stimulation paradigms are considered. Machine learning testing accuracy from wired and our new wireless system shows < 8% difference in Whisker and fore limb stimulations. Our wireless system also indicates successful detection of biopotential signals as low as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15\ \mu V_{pp}$</tex>. These findings support the premise that the proposed real-time machine interface is effective for wireless and battery-free acquisition of biopotentials. Given this development, system evaluation and classification can be pursued for future clinical research.

articleTitle: New Thermal Emission Effects in Temporal Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: So far, most of the developments on thermal radiation, essentially aimed at enhancing the control of its propagation and spectral properties, have mainly been based on the use of photonic nanostructures. Within this context, a new emerging field of research are temporal metamaterials. Given the realized successes of this new paradigm, and the manifest parallelism between the areas of photonics and thermal emission, it seems reasonable to think that temporal metamaterials could also revolutionize the field of thermal radiation, both at fundamental and applied levels. However, such an approach, merging thermal emission and time-varying media, has remained quite elusive, and the underlying physics has scarcely been explored as yet. Hence, in this work, we put forward a quantum theoretical framework that sets a rigorous basis to address thermal emission in time-modulated materials. Upon this ground, we unveil new physics, showing the occurrence of non-local correlations, the potential of temporal metamaterials to radiate outside the black-body spectrum, as well as the existence of quantum vacuum amplification effects at finite temperature. Finally, we show how these features may lead to novel thermal emission effects as well as the conception of innovative thermal emitters dual to spatial gratings.

articleTitle: On the Fast Direct Solution of Low-Frequency Integral Formulations via Operator Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, new fast direct solvers for integral equations are introduced. These solvers are designed to operate in the low-to-moderate frequency range and are built on top of preconditioned first-kind operators or second-kind operators that are further regularized using Laplacian filters.
