The filtering tackles two issues that make fast direct solvers so challenging to obtain in the first place: spectral errors that occur during boundary element discretization are effectively dealt, and, consequently, a low-rank representation for compact perturbations of all relevant operators can be obtained. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of these approaches in directly solving integral equations.

articleTitle: Considerations for Antenna Design and Signal Processing in Radar-Based Hallway Gait Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this study, we examined the use of commercially available radars for monitoring gait in hallways. To address the challenges of this task, we evaluated two approaches: 1) modifying the radar antenna using a hyperbolic lens and 2) a novel signal processing method. For the first approach, we designed an add-on lens to improve the beam focus of a commercial radar system. For the second approach, we proposed an algorithm that can be used with any type of MIMO FMCW radar to detect human gait in a hallway without requiring modifications to the radar antenna. Our results showed that both methods were able to extract gait values with similar accuracy, but the signal processing method was computationally intensive, while the antenna modification method required less computational power.

articleTitle: 4D Radar Imaging for Target Detection Using Cascaded Transceiver: Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Automotive industries are moving towards providing automated driving experience which encourages many developers to design and develop MIMO-based FMCW radar imaging with cascaded multi-chip architecture. This paper presents a multi-chip high-resolution radar imaging with high range-resolution for object detection and localization. The Retina-4F radar developed by Smart Radar System allows the system to provide real-time information of the target in terms of localization, doppler velocity, FFT power amplitude and point cloud data. In this work, we demonstrate a few test performances to evaluate the performance of the radar in detecting and localizing pedestrians, motorcycle, and car. The data are collected by varying the test scenario which includes multiple target and different size target. The radar operates in 77GHz frequency while the test environment is done at an open area with a controlled test space. Through the result obtained, the detection and localization of the targets are explained and discussed for further work.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Electromagnetic Analysis of Scattering on Rough Surfaces of Arctic Sea Ice in the Presence of Oil Contamination Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Detecting oil in sea ice is an important issue that has gained attention as transportation increases the risk of a spill in the warming Arctic environment. Remote sensing model studies can provide insight into the conditions for which microwave scattering is affected by the introduction of oil in sea ice. In this work, we demonstrate a model framework based on the Surface-Volume-Surface Electric Field Integral Equation (SVSEFIE) Method and contrast its results with the commercially available FEKO code. Case studies on newly-formed sea ice and oil-covered first year sea ice were conducted at L-band (1.5 GHz). Results showed that L-band was sensitive to the presence of an oil layer on the sea ice and excellent agreement between the modeling techniques was achieved.

articleTitle: Concave Body-Surface Curvature Influence on the On-Body Path Gain - A Numerical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: The influence of concave surface curvature on the on-body path gain for wireless body area networks is investigated numerically through simulations. A concave dielectric slab configuration, with two S-band open-ended waveguide antennas placed at each end of the slab, is simulated for different values of the curvature. The effect of surface wave propagation is attempted isolated by simulation of a reference configuration where the concave part of the structure is replaced by vacuum. Certain required parameters of the reference configuration, i.e., edge smoothness and flat slab lengths, are determined through a subset of parameter sweeps. It is found that the path gain initially increases to a maximum and subsequently decreases as the curvature changes from a completely flat section to a 90 degrees bend. It was not possible to distinguish the effect of the surface waves on the on-body path gain from a possible approach of a null in the antenna radiation patterns as the path gain reached its minimum for increasing curvatures.

articleTitle: Observations of a Terrestrial Snowfall Event on Grassland Using Polarimetric Microwave Radars
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Microwave remote sensing is an indispensable tool for monitoring snow. Several studies have been conducted on observing snow cover and its characteristics. In this study, we examine the potential ability of L-band and C-band microwave radars to detect snow on land. To achieve this, co-polarized and cross-polarized signals were obtained before and after a snowfall event occurred. We analyzed the normalized radar cross sections (NRCS) of C- and L-band scatterometers during the total period of study. Results showed that L- and C-bands were not able to detect snow on the ground immediately; however, they were sensitive to the changing snowpack parameters induced by environmental conditions. The results were most sensitive to the variation of snowpack parameters at low incidence angles.

articleTitle: Polarization-Selective Fano-Resonance in Cascaded Frequency-Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this work we investigate a cascaded system of two symmetric frequency-selective surfaces (FSSs) that supports a Fano resonance (FR) at off-normal incidence in the millimeter-wave range. The first FSS is shaped with the four-arms star, and the second FSS is based on the quasi-square geometry. These two single-layer FSSs present resonant frequencies at 28 GHz (FSS #1) and 36 GHz (FSS #2). Cascading of the two FSSs was realized by using an air gap of 2.5 mm. The FSS prototypes were fabricated and measured in an anechoic chamber. It is demonstrated that a single FR is excited when the symmetry of the overall cascaded element is broken at an incidence of θ ≥ 20°.

articleTitle: Design of Spatially-Dispersive Huygens Meta-Atoms for Non-Local Phase-Gradient Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe the design and possible applications of spatially-dispersive Huygens meta-atoms. Such structures, consisting of patterned metal sheets separated by dielectric layers, are engineered to exhibit full transmission for multiple incidence angles and a desired angular spectrum of the phase insertion function. It is also shown how these spatially-dispersive meta-atoms can be used to implement non-local phase-gradient metasurfaces introducing a different beam-steering effect depending on the incidence angle of the impinging wave. The proposed structures, which are fully passive and do not require any reconfigurable element, may find application in a variety of modern wireless devices, such as functionalized meta-domes for antennas or electromagnetic skins for non-line-of-sight radio links.

articleTitle: Four-Element Reconfigurable UWB-MIMO Antenna with Band-Reject Capability
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, a compact four-element reconfigurable ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with WiMAX band-notched characteristics is investigated. The proposed antenna comprises of four modified disc-shaped radiating elements, etched on top of the FR-4 substrate and excited with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50 \Omega$</tex> micro-strip feeding line. While the bottom layer has a common defected ground plane in which a meandered line slot, a rectangular slot and four quasi-selfcomplementary (QSC) slots are loaded. The overall volume of the proposed antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$39 \times 39 \times 0.8 \ \text{mm} 3$</tex>. To achieve the satisfactory inter-element isolation as well as compactness, all the elements are positioned in the orthogonal arrangement. In addition, a decoupling structure is also added to control the unwanted interelement surface waves coupling. Further, to obtain a reconfigurable band-rejection capability in the proposed UWB-MIMO antenna, four different PIN diodes are embedded on reverse 2 -shaped slot of each radiator. In case 1, all the PIN diodes are in OFF state, the simulated reflection coefficients (S11= S22= S33= S44) are less than - 10 dB over 2.62 to 10.74 GHz with inter-element isolation (between diagonal and adjacent elements) is more than 13 dB, whereas in case 2, when all the PIN diodes are in ON state, the simulated reflection coefficients (S11= S22= S33= S44) are less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{- 1 0 \ d B \ o v e r \ }$</tex> 2.62 to 11.92 GHz frequencies except at 3.23 to 3.81 GHz (rejecting Wi-MAX band), and the simulated inter-port isolation (between diagonal and adjacent elements) is greater than 15 dB. Furthermore, to ensure the usefulness of the proposed antenna for upcoming wireless applications, diversity performance parameters such as Envelope Correlation Coefficients (ECC) and Diversity Gain (DG) have also been reviewed and found satisfactory.

articleTitle: Comparison of Asymptotic Far-Fields of Magnetic Dipole Antennas with Loop Versus Spherical Current Densities
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A recent analysis has examined a new variety of magnetic antenna design, in which an azimuthal electric current flows within a spherical shell with a density that is proportional to the sine function of the spherical polar angle. This previous investigation yielded exact forms for the electro-magnetic (EM) fields for all space, including the regions exterior as well as interior to the sphere. This solution was expressed as a simple product of an associate Legendre polynomial, a spherical Bessel function, and an exponential function. In the present analysis, the asymptotic forms of the electric and magnetic fields are examined in the far-field. In particular, these field profiles for the subject spherical current density are compared with that of conventional circular loop antennas that are characterized by the same radius and total current. In addition, the field pattern of the subject spherical current density is stable with regards to different radio frequency (RF) wavelengths. In contrast, circular loop antennas can exhibit significant field pattern variation with regards to wavelength, especially if the RF wavelength is much less than the loop radius.

articleTitle: Real-Time 3D Microwave Tomography of Brain Stroke Status Using Low-Computing Demand
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: This paper approaches the medical problem of the after-onset monitoring of a brain stroke via a real-time linear imaging algorithm and a low-complexity microwave scanner. This procedure allows using low computing requirements for tracking physical pathology changes, such as stroke shape evolution and the partial typology variation of the infarcted zones, both significant medical issues. The system consists of a 22-antenna device, and the imaging algorithm uses a differential single-frequency approach. It exploits a pair of measured scattering matrices taken at two different instants, the Born approximation, and the truncated singular value decomposition, to form in-time 3D tomographic dielectric contrast variation maps in real-time using a stand-alone low-capacity device without needing a graphics processing unit. The results confirm the continuous stroke follow-up capabilities of the system, with the possibility to track both the shape and type transformations (hemorrhage and ischemia), even in mimicked complex clinical scenarios.

articleTitle: An Implicit IE-GSTC Metasurface Forward Solver
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We present the formulation of a novel integral-equation (IE)-based algorithm to solve for the scattered fields of a metasurface problem. The metasurface is assumed to be a thin sheet behaving according to the susceptibility model from the generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs). The proposed (implicit) IE-GSTC algorithm differs from other IE-GSTC methods by solving for the average scattered fields (by utilizing the mathematical properties of the IE operators) and only indirectly using the GSTC equations, which results in a reduced number of fundamental unknowns when compared to other methods. In addition, we show how the average scattered fields can be used in order to find the scattered fields everywhere. The proposed method is used to simulate two cases under the two-dimensional transverse-electric assumption. In particular, the results of the second case are compared to those obtained by a full-wave simulation in ANSYS HFSS.

articleTitle: Fast and Low-Cost Design of Wideband Reflectarrays for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A low-cost 3D-printed reflectarray is proposed in this paper. The reflectarray (16 × 32 unit cells) consists of a layer of patches and a 3D-printed layer covered by copper tape that functions as a ground plane backing. In this study, the structure that serves as a reflectarray for 5G millimeter-wave frequencies is designed using a low-cost fabrication technique. A wideband operation of 20 GHz to 42 GHz can be observed based on the reflection phase and return loss. Prototypes are fabricated and provide a good agreement between the simulated and measured radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Chip Package-PCB Interconnect Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A systematic approach to reduce the differential return loss of interconnects in very high-speed high-density chip- package-board system is presented. Optimization is performed using Ansys HFSS 3D EM simulator, first in parts, and then with the end-to-end interconnect. Numerical results show values that are realizable and highlight regions that are challenging.

Author Keywords: s-parameters of packages and printed circuit boards

articleTitle: Field Intensity Shaping via Linear Superposition of Elementary Focused Patterns
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this contribution, the field intensity shaping is addressed. This problem is relevant in several applications, including hyperthermia treatment planning, magnetic resonance radiofrequency shimming, satellite and radio communications, as well as in antenna array synthesis theory. The aim is the design of the array complex excitations such to ensure uniform and maximum field intensity distribution inside a given region of interest, while keeping it under control in some other regions. To this end, a three steps procedure is proposed, which involves the superposition of single focused patterns and the minimization of the nuclear norm.

articleTitle: TEM-Mode in an Elliptic Coaxial Waveguide with Impedance-Matched RHM to LHM Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this paper, we perform analytical and numerical studies of TEM-wave propagation in an elliptic coaxial waveguide filled with a graded inhomogeneous RHM-LHM composite. Within the composite, the real parts of the effective permittivity and permeability vary along the propagation direction (chosen to be the z-direction) according to a hyperbolic tangent function. The present model introduces the transition width as an additional degree of freedom in the graded metamaterial composite design, which allows for tailoring of the electromagnetic wave propagation. An excellent agreement is obtained between the analytical results and numerical results obtained using the COMSOL Multiphysics software.

articleTitle: Low Cost Intelligent Reflective Surfaces Using Mechatronic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) is one of the revolutionary technology due to their capability to dynamically manipulate electromagnetic waves (EM). Those capabilities to achieve such characteristics are by incorporating active elements into the metasurface design. Although intelligent reflective surfaces are such a promising solution for future wireless communications, each unit cell of the metasurface requires at least one active device. This led to high costs, complexity in design, and signal disruptions. Here, we proposed intelligent reflective surfaces by utilizing mechanical actuators with beam-scanning capability. The proposed IRSs are designed based on the phase-modulated metasurface unit cell and by using the rotation of the unit cell and spatial gap of supercells, the reflected beam can be controlled. The gear matrix and power screw systems are introduced as the mechanical actuator.

articleTitle: Wirelessly Enabled Beam Steering MSF Antenna for Biomedical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: In this work, a wirelessly enabled beam steering metasurface (MSF) antenna for bio-imaging is proposed. The design consists of multiple layers, the top layer consists of an MSF layer, while the bottom layer consists of two layers, one that contains the feeding antennas and the second consists of the feeding network. In the feeding network of the MSF antenna, an RF energy harvesting (EH) system has been incorporated that allows dynamic switching to achieve the desired beam steering required for torso scanning. In the designed EH system, a receiving antenna and rectifying circuit harvests the low power received RF signal at three different frequencies in the 2.4 GHz ISM band. In order to avoid coupling between the EH system and MSF antenna, the former operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, while the latter operates in the 900 MHz ISM band. The proposed approach has potential to be used in biomedical imaging applications and to provide an alternative to complex biasing networks required to reconfigure devices.

articleTitle: Hybrid 1D Maxwell-Schrödinger Modeling of Dispersive Regime Effects of a Transmon Qubit
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Transmon qubits integrated into microwave circuitry are a leading quantum computing architecture. However, significant engineering improvements are still needed. General-purpose numerical methods are becoming of interest to tackle these challenges, but existing fully-quantum methods are highly inefficient. In this work, we formulate a semiclassical Maxwell-Schrödinger model as an alternative approach to efficiently analyze the interactions of transmons capacitively coupled to transmission line networks. Additionally, we present a suitable discretization and time marching strategy. We validate our approach by comparing it to theoretical models relevant to the dispersive operating regime used in most hardware implementations. Our results show that our method can accurately predict effects related to transmon state measurements that are typically derived using fully-quantum models. In the future, our approach can be used to rapidly explore broader design spaces to improve the speed and fidelity of qubit state measurements, which is a key obstacle toward achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Impedance Matching of a Planar Patch Antenna Phased Array Using Split-Ring Based Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A method for reducing the variation of the reflection coefficient with scan angle of a patch antenna phased array using a split-ring loaded dielectric (SRLD) sheet is proposed. Loading a thin dielectric sheet with SRs enables the effective susceptance of the sheet to be tuned. Equalizing the array reflection coefficient is achieved by providing the required susceptance at a certain distance in front of the array face using the sheet. Simulation results for a uniform 9 × 9 element patch antenna phased array, compensated using this method, are presented. Using this metasurface, the scanning range with active VSWR less than 2.5 is increased from ±53° to ±64° in the E plane, and from ±36° to ±65° in the H plane.

articleTitle: Investigating the Performance of Cascaded Metasurfaces with Physically Realizable Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: We investigate how the performance of a cascaded metasurface system can change when it is designed with physically realizable unit cells as opposed to unit cells based on impedance boundary conditions. In the provided example, we have observed that the performance of the physically realizable metasurface system has degraded significantly close to its edges.

articleTitle: UAV Detection & Classification Aided by Full-Wave Electromagnetic CAD Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: Range Doppler (RD) imaging is a technique utilized for the detection and classification of Unmanned Air Vehicles (UAVs). The effectiveness of RD images is influenced by the operating frequency and bandwidth of the radar system. In this study, the impact of utilizing various radars with different frequency bands on the accuracy of RD images of a spinning blade was investigated using full-wave electromagnetic computer-aided design software. The simulated radars were selected to align with some commonly used radars in the field of UAV detection and classification. Results showed that mmWave radars, due to their broad bandwidth, exhibited the highest RD accuracy among the other radar systems examined.

articleTitle: A Charging Nest Made of Novel Dish-Backed Yagi-Uda Antennas for Misalignment-Resilient Wireless Power Transfer for Drone Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 URSI International Symposium on Electromagnetic Theory (EMTS)
abstract: A misalignment-resilient wireless power system is proposed. This system, referred to as a pill-shaped nest is made of a circular array of dish-backed Yagi-Uda antennas to operate at 433 MHz. The circular array allows for the concentration of the electric and magnetic field at the center of the nest to rapidly charge swarms of drones. The antennas are designed and simulated at 433 MHz and exhibit high efficiency even under the influence of 3 degrees of lateral misalignment. The results suggest that a wireless power efficiency of up to 85% can be achieved for misalignment distances of up to 17 cm, The low-profile, misalignment-resilient, and cost-efficient aspects of the system combined with its ability to power a variety of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and its ability to be placed at any location make it appealing to any UAV system with charging needs. These results constitute the first step in tackling the issue of extended flight time for drones as they are being used for crucial operations like package delivery, disaster relief and rescue, law enforcement, and military operations as well as any other systems in need of wireless, fast, and continuous charging.
